subject: PERFORM statement
notes: UNTIL EXIT binds to PerformForever and renders `while (true) { body }` - a condition-1 that never evaluates true, exactly GR11. Edition: Annex E.3.3 item 37 ('The PERFORM statement now allows the UNTIL EXIT phrase which causes an infinite loop') makes it a 2023 addition; MEASURED at --std 2014 the construct gate rejects it (COBOL0900 citing §14.9.28.2 until-phrase / §14.9.28.4 GR11), and at 2023 it compiles. NOTE 4's escapes MEASURED: gr11_inline_exit - EXIT PERFORM leaves the loop while EXIT PERFORM CYCLE only re-iterates (N=04 CYCLED=01); gr11_exit_paragraph - an out-of-line `PERFORM SUBP UNTIL EXIT` whose SUBP ends in EXIT PARAGRAPH does NOT escape (it looped to N=4 and left only via STOP RUN), which is the case NOTE 4 warns about.
